messages:
mike: quick ping — PR #8429 (service: routing) is green and ready but blocked on architecture review. RFC linked: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/130-kv-cache-routing. can someone from arch take a look? cc @tara @alan

tara: skimmed the RFC earlier — overall looks reasonable. two quick q's: 1) will the canary span regions or be single-region? 2) what's the fallback path for quantized variants?

mike: answers: 1) single region for now (us-west-2) to keep blast radius small. 2) fallback to model-variant v1 (fp16) with automatic routing. added a config snippet in the PR:```yaml
canary:
  region: us-west-2
  fallback:
    model_variant: v1
  rollout: [10,50,100]
```

alan: ack — we require arch signoff before merging. i'll review today; please add a short test plan in PR description (load + latency guardrails).

joel: added a brief test plan and attached the sample canary logs to the PR (small run, ~200 requests).

arch-bot: Arch review required: add `arch-approved` label to PR after @alan confirms. Current labels: [needs-arch-review, canary-ready]

mike: thanks @alan — ping when you can. if it's helpful I can split the telemetry rename into a separate PR to speed merge. ETA EOD for responses.

alan: reviewed — left two small comments about telemetry key naming and a missing metric tag. no arch blockers. @mike please address those and i'll add arch-approved then.

mike: fixed the telemetry keys and pushed a new commit. replied to your comments.

tara: quicklook — lgtm from product/ops perspective. nice to have the small rollback plan in the PR too. :thumbsup:

alan: adding arch-approved label now, removing `needs-arch-review` gate. go ahead and merge after CI passes.

mike: merging once CI finishes. thanks everyone!
